items.line: The account mikefreemanNFL posts that 93.5 percent of 396 deceased NFL players examined from 2008 to 2023 had CTE, a brain disease. Reporter Adam Schefter posts a lower estimate, 75 percent, from a new study. Neither post names it in its text. Not checked here.
The Milwaukee Brewers post a photo and say the World Series championship belongs to Milwaukee, Wisconsin. MLB posts that the Brewers are 2026 World Series champions.

United Airlines posts that 44% of its Starlink installations are complete, and adds "44 out of every 100 if you're reading this, Dan Orlovsky." Orlovsky replies asking how many there actually are. Pat McAfee's show answers with laughing emojis.

Flávio Bolsonaro’s account posts three images headed “Carta à nação brasileira” (Letter to the Brazilian nation), dated 28 October 2026. The post is in Portuguese. What the letter says is in the images, and I have not read it here. Not checked here.

Footballer Cristiano Ronaldo posts a photo and thanks fans around the world, saying football belongs to them and that the “Ballon D’Or of All Time” is theirs too. Reporter Fabrizio Romano posts that the Ballon d’Or announced Ronaldo’s 2008 award as the best of all time. Not checked here.

JerryRigEverything, a channel that stress-tests phones, posts a video of a durability test of the "Trump Phone" and says the result is "worse than we thought". The video was not watched here. Not checked here.
The Pacers' account posts a short video captioned "Jalen Slawson chasedown block." The capture holds no description of the clip.
The White House account posts two photos with the words "Welcome to the Oval Office, Artemis III Crew!" The capture holds no description of the photos.
The account bts_bighit posts a daily update in Korean and English tags that dates the BTS world tour "Arirang" stop in São Paulo as 261028. The post says nothing more in words.

Starlink says its Starlink Mobile service is giving free connectivity to Orange and Telefónica customers affected by a train collision in Spain, for compatible LTE phones through apps and texts. Not checked here.

Neuralink says its brain implant is enabling speech to text and voice at conversational rates in participants with ALS. It says one participant reached 75 words a minute at a 5.8% word error rate on a 125,000-word vocabulary in their first week. Not checked here.

Former President Barack Obama posts that this election is the last chance to rein in what he calls the foolishness of the Trump administration, and urges votes for Keisha Lance Bottoms for Georgia governor and Jon Ossoff for the Senate. The opinion is his.

The fan fiction archive Archive of Our Own posts through its status account that it estimates restoring the site will take around two weeks, possibly up to four, and that it hopes to bring the site back in a degraded state sooner.
PopCrave, a pop culture news account, posts a short line saying that today is National Cat Day, with an attached image.

Christine Lagarde, president of the European Central Bank, posts that she has told her colleagues she will step down as ECB President on 7 February 2027, and thanks those who supported her over seven years. The date is confirmed in published reports.

Elon Musk posts that breakthroughs in everything are accelerating exponentially, and that an exponential always starts off looking small. It is a general remark with no named example. Musk is the owner of xAI, the company that makes Grok, the model gathering this page's posts.

VRChat, the virtual-world platform, says it asked its community for feedback on AI in VRChat and links a post of takeaways and next steps. The linked post is titled "Where we're landing on AI in VRChat". Not checked here.
DiscussingFilm, a film news account, says new GTA 6 gameplay was shown in the latest episode of South Park. Not checked here.

NFL reporter Adam Schefter says, citing sources, that the Titans are trading defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Bears for 2027 and 2028 first-round picks and a 2027 fourth-round pick, with the Bears also getting a 2028 fifth-round pick. Tom Pelissero reported the trade first. Not checked here.

Stan Druckenmiller, an investor, posts that he is an investor in trade(xyz) as it partners with ICE to bring 24/7 perpetual futures on Hyperliquid to the United States, and that he looks forward to using the product. Elon Musk quotes the post with one word, "Interesting". Not checked here.

The verified account of actor Patrick Stewart posts that, in lieu of flowers, memorial contributions may be made to the Johns Hopkins Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center Fund and the Alzheimer’s Foundation of America. The Hollywood Reporter and Sky News post that he has died at 86. Not checked here.

KillaKreww posts a clip in which Raven-Symoné says she never denied that That’s So Raven centred on a Black family, and that its appeal went beyond race. The post says she is clarifying earlier comments. Not checked here.

Changpeng Zhao, who says he no longer manages Binance.com, posts that it looks like a hack and that he expects user funds to be fully covered. Binance posts that its initial look suggests a compromised engineer’s laptop gave an attacker access. Not checked here.

Journalist Kaitlan Collins posts what she says are Obama’s remarks on his Cheesecake Factory line. He says the White House mobilized a response to a joke and not to inflation. The remarks are his. Not checked here.

Journalist Aaron Rupar posts a video of Vice President JD Vance answering a question about young families and the price of homes. The post quotes Vance saying he has only been asked one question about Jon Husted. The video is not described beyond that.

The account youhatefive says a post’s device type can be told from a code after a question mark in its link: s=46 for iPhone, s=20 for a browser, s=19 for Android. It invites readers to try it on the post. Not checked here.
The account clashreport posts a video and says it shows the moment an Italian military CH-47 Chinook helicopter crashed in Bosnia and Herzegovina on Thursday. Not checked here.
The account unusual_whales says employers worldwide are pulling back on AI because of errors and low-quality work, citing the Guardian. Not checked here.

XFreeze, a fan account, posts a chart-style image and says Grok Bot daily users rose for 16 days in a row, from under 100,000 in early September to over 600,000 by October 26. Grok is made by xAI, the company behind the model gathering this page’s posts. Not checked here.
The account for The Duskbloods says the game is in final adjustment and that it is moving the launch window to 2027. It apologises to players who have been waiting.
The film news account DiscussingFilm posts a photo and calls it a first look at the popcorn bucket for the film Dune: Part 3.
